name: styles
title: Design tokens and themes
description: The token contract every component renders against.

definition.base/border.yaml:
$description: Border widths. Border COLOR is semantic (see themes/*.json color.border.*).
border:
  width:
    $type: dimension
    none:
      $value: "0"
    thin:
      $value: 1px
    thick:
      $value: 2px
    heavy:
      $description: A deliberate outline that reads as a shape in its own right, not a hairline separator — the CtaLink pill's rule. Part of the shared scale so an atom in rx/marketplace can use it; every org inherits this width and may override it.
      $value: 4px

definition.base/typography.yaml:
$description: "Typographic primitives — the GLOBAL DESIGN SYSTEM type scale (apps/design-system/storybook/styles), token-for-token: Inter family, fluid clamp() sizes per role, weights, per-role line-heights + letter-spacing. Semantic text styles (semantic/text-styles.json) compose these by role; components reference the semantic role, never these primitives. (The flat xs–5xl scale + tight/snug/normal aliases remain for the generic size/lineHeight style keys.)"
font:
  family:
    $type: fontFamily
    sans:
      $value:
        - Inter
        - system-ui
        - -apple-system
        - Segoe UI
        - Roboto
        - Helvetica
        - Arial
        - sans-serif
    mono:
      $value:
        - ui-monospace
        - SFMono-Regular
        - Menlo
        - Consolas
        - monospace
    display:
      $description: Display/heading family — defaults to the body stack; an org overrides THIS (one token) to rebrand every heading.
      $value:
        - Inter
        - system-ui
        - -apple-system
        - Segoe UI
        - Roboto
        - Helvetica
        - Arial
        - sans-serif
    prose:
      $description: Long-form HEADING family (semantic/text-styles.json's prose.* styles). Defaults to the display face, because for most orgs the heading face IS the display face. An org whose display face is a poster face (single weight, uppercase, tight) overrides THIS one token rather than re-declaring the prose styles, because such a face is unreadable over a page of copy while remaining right on a hero.
      $value: "{font.family.display}"
  size:
    $type: dimension
    xs:
      $value: 0.75rem
    sm:
      $value: 0.875rem
    base:
      $value: 1rem
    lg:
      $value: 1.125rem
    xl:
      $value: 1.25rem
    2xl:

    display:

definition.semantic/app-sizes.yaml:
$description: STANDARD APP SIZES — the named width blocks `appWidth` can reference (docs/design/05). DATA, served on the theme (theme.appSize) and resolved by the SDK like any token; values are raw host-facing CSS (the one token home where that is the point). Every size carries a viewport ceiling — min(100vw, …) — so no panel ever exceeds the screen, and the app never takes over the host page (sizes are bounded, never fill). chat = the core conversational surface (a panel that is always open) · chat-slim = the narrow chat used when a voice panel/focus surface is open beside it · rail = a narrow stacked-cards slide-out · panel = a full detail/form slide-out.
appSize:
  chat:
    $value: min(100vw, 680px)
  chat-slim:
    $value: min(100vw, 480px)
  rail:
    $value: min(100vw, 360px)
  panel:
    $value: min(100vw, 600px)
definition.semantic/fonts.yaml:
$description: Default webfonts — Inter (the declared font.family.sans), loaded from Google Fonts. Served as theme.fonts; the SDK injects a <link> per URL at document level.

    $value: [ https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap ]
definition.semantic/grid.yaml:
$description: >-
  Grid behaviour as DATA. `stackBelow` is the width at which a columns grid gives up and
  stacks — every child goes full width, one per row. It lives here rather than in the SDK
  because it is a value, and the SDK owns none: an org that wants its grids to hold their
  shape longer overrides this ONE token. A grid may still override it per-instance with
  `style.stackBelow`.
grid:
  stackBelow:
    $type: dimension
    $value: "{space.120}"

definition.semantic/keyframes.yaml:
$description: Named keyframe animations as DATA. The SDK serializes these into CSS @keyframes (uno-<name>) once per render root; any definition animates by referencing one via `style.animation` — no SDK edit, no per-animation primitive. Stop keys are CSS keyframe selectors; decls use real CSS property names in KEBAB-CASE ("box-shadow", never "boxShadow") — lint-enforced, guarded by server/tests/rx/keyframes-contract.test.ts, because this file is the one animation contract every renderer (web SDK, Studio, future Flutter/RN/iOS) parses. `wave` is the thinking-dots bob, grounded in legacy ChatHistoryItem.module.css (waveFloat).
keyframes:
  wave:
    $value:
      0%,100%:
        transform: translateY(0)
        opacity: "0.4"
      50%:
        transform: translateY(-6px)
        opacity: "1"
  focusFadeIn:
    $value:
      from:
        opacity: "0"
        transform: scale(0.98)
      to:
        opacity: "1"
        transform: scale(1)
  pulseRing:
    $value:
      0%:
        transform: scale(0.92)
        opacity: "0.45"
      70%:
        opacity: "0.08"
      100%:
        transform: scale(1.9)
        opacity: "0"
  slideUp:
    $value:
      from:
        opacity: "0"
        transform: translateY(20px)
      to:
        opacity: "1"
        transform: translateY(0)
  breathe:
    $value:
      0%,100%:
        transform: scale(1)
      50%:
        transform: scale(1.08)
  dotPulse:
    $value:
      0%,100%:
        transform: scale(1)
        opacity: "1"
      50%:
        transform: scale(1.4)
        opacity: "0.5"
  slideInRight:
    $value:
      from:
        transform: translateX(100%)
      to:
        transform: translateX(0)
  kenBurns:
    $value:
      0%,100%:
        transform: scale(1) translate(0, 0)
      50%:
        transform: scale(1.12) translate(-1.5%, 1%)
definition.semantic/layout.yaml:
$description: >-
  PAGE WIDTHS, named. These are aliases onto the same space scale, not a second scale: the
  point is that a page-level cap reads as what it IS ("maxWidth: reading") instead of a
  number you have to convert (40rem). The band starts at 30rem because that is where a
  width stops being an element and starts being a page.

  THE RULE, so one value never gets two spellings: a PAGE-level cap (maxWidth on a content
  container, a hideBelow/stackBelow threshold) uses a NAME here; an ELEMENT's own size
  (an image tile's height, a card's max) stays a scale step. Element sizes are not page
  widths and must not borrow these words.
layout:
  $type: dimension
  compact:
    $description: 30rem / 480px — the narrowest a page column gets before it stacks.
    $value: "{space.120}"
  narrow:
    $value: "{space.140}"
  reading:
    $description: 40rem / 640px — a comfortable measure for a column of prose.
    $value: "{space.160}"
  page:
    $description: 45rem / 720px — the standard content container.
    $value: "{space.180}"
  wide:
    $value: "{space.200}"
definition.semantic/orb.yaml:
$description: >-
  The orb's INK — the colour the Orb primitive draws its light in, depth-shaded as it
  paints. Graphite by deliberate default, because an orb is ambient presence rather than
  an action and must never compete with the face or content it sits behind; a brand action
  colour reads as an alarm at this size. Three weights are offered so a surface can pick
  how present the orb should be, plus a brand tint for the rare surface that wants one.
  SEMANTIC rather than per-theme, so every org inherits these and none has to redeclare
  them (the theme contract binds theme files only), and one value serves both themes
  because the primitive lightens the ink on dark substrates. An org retints every orb it
  ships by overriding these names, with no effect on text or action colours.
color:
  $type: color
  orb:
    ink:
      $value: "{color.gray.500}"
    ink-soft:
      $value: "{color.gray.400}"
    ink-faint:
      $value: "{color.gray.300}"
    brand:
      $value: "{color.action.primary}"
definition.semantic/prose.yaml:
$description: Markdown primitive element styling — DATA, served at theme.prose. The Markdown SDK primitive READS this and applies it; it authors nothing. Grounded in the legacy prose.css. Values reference tokens.
prose:
  paragraph:
    $value:
      margin: 0 0 0.75em 0
      lineHeight: "1.5"
  link:
    $value:
      color: "{color.action.primary}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.bold}"
      textDecoration: none
  linkIcon:
    $value:
      width: 0.85em
      height: 0.85em
      display: inline-block
      verticalAlign: middle
      marginLeft: 0.1em
      marginBottom: 0.1em
  # Steps and contact/benefit lists are what long-form copy is mostly made of, so markers
  # sit close to the text and rows breathe. A tighter indent than the 1.5rem this started
  # at: markdown mostly renders inside a CARD, where a deep indent costs a fifth of the line.
  list:
    $value:
      margin: "{space.3} 0"
      paddingLeft: 1.25rem
  listItem:
    $value:
      margin: "{space.1} 0"
      paddingLeft: "{space.1}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.relaxed}"
  bulletStyle:
    $value: disc
  orderedStyle:
    $value: decimal
  tableWrap:
    $value:
      width: 100%
      overflowX: auto
      border: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
      borderRadius: "{radius.lg}"
      margin: "{space.3} 0"
  table:
    $value:
      width: 100%
      borderCollapse: collapse
  cell:
    $value:
      padding: "{space.1} {space.2}"
      textAlign: left
      verticalAlign: top
      borderBottom: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
  headerCell:
    $value:
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
      background: "{color.surface.sunken}"
      color: "{color.text.primary}"
  # INLINE MARKS and BLOCKS. Authored copy uses all of these: a bolded access code, a rule
  # between sections, a quoted term, a reference number set as code. Before these existed
  # the Markdown primitive had no recipe key for them, so they rendered at the browser's
  # default, which is the one way a definition's look escapes the token layer entirely.
  # WEIGHT ONLY, NO COLOUR. An inline mark is drawn INSIDE whatever it emphasises, and the
  # recipes are inline styles with no nesting context — so a colour asserted here beats the
  # colour of the thing it sits in. Bolding a link's anchor text (`[**Applied Knowledge**](…)`
  # — the shape the markdown guidelines ask for, since they bold product names AND link first
  # mentions) turned the words `text.primary` while the link's arrow, a direct child of the
  # anchor, stayed on the link colour: one bubble cobalt, the next one black, same theme
  # (observed live 2026-08-14). Inheriting is also the correct answer everywhere else: bold
  # in body copy takes the body's colour, bold in a quote takes the quote's. Colour belongs
  # to the CONTEXT; an inline mark contributes weight.
  strong:
    $value:
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
  emphasis:
    $value:
      fontStyle: italic
  strikethrough:
    $value:
      textDecoration: line-through
      color: "{color.text.tertiary}"
  # Inline: a reference, an access code, a rate. Sized in em so it sits with its line.
  code:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.mono}"
      fontSize: 0.9em
      padding: "0.1em 0.3em"
      background: "{color.surface.sunken}"
      border: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
      borderRadius: "{radius.sm}"
      color: "{color.text.primary}"
  # Block: scrolls rather than wrapping, because a wrapped code block is unreadable and a
  # widened one breaks the card it sits in.
  codeBlock:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.mono}"
      fontSize: 0.875em
      margin: "{space.5} 0"
      padding: "{space.4}"
      background: "{color.surface.sunken}"
      border: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
      borderRadius: "{radius.lg}"
      overflowX: auto
  blockquote:
    $value:
      margin: "{space.5} 0"
      paddingLeft: "{space.4}"
      borderLeft: "{border.width.thick} solid {color.border.strong}"
      color: "{color.text.secondary}"
  # A `---` between sections. Quieter than a section heading's rule, which carries its own.
  rule:
    $value:
      border: none
      borderTop: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
      margin: "{space.8} 0"

  image:
    $value:
      maxWidth: 100%
      height: auto
      display: block
      margin: "{space.3} 0"
      borderRadius: "{radius.lg}"
      border: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
  imageFallback:
    $value:
      color: "{color.text.tertiary}"
  # Headings point at the PROSE type styles (semantic/text-styles.json), never at the UI
  # scale: a heading in a body of copy carries the margins and the section rule that a card
  # title must never carry. h4 and below share one label style, because copy that needs four
  # levels of hierarchy has a writing problem rather than a token problem.
  heading:
    $value:
      h1: prose.section
      h2: prose.section
      h3: prose.subsection
      h4: prose.label
      h5: prose.label
      h6: prose.label
definition.semantic/root.yaml:
$description: Base render-root settings the SDK spreads onto its OUTERMOST wrapper on every render path (component AND app) — whole-tree normalization served as DATA, the Unoverse equivalent of the design-system's Shadow-DOM baseline (.gravity-component reset). It sets the DS typography (font family/size/weight/line-height/colour) so every node inherits it without a per-component style; the SDK authors none of these values — they reference the typography + colour tokens.
root:
  $value:
    WebkitFontSmoothing: antialiased
    MozOsxFontSmoothing: grayscale
    fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
    fontSize: "{font.size.bodyMd}"
    fontWeight: "{font.weight.normal}"
    lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.normal}"
    letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.normal}"
    color: "{color.text.primary}"
definition.semantic/skeleton.yaml:
$description: Skeleton (loading placeholder) recipe as DATA — the SDK's SkeletonView only LOOKS THIS UP, it authors no dimensions. `bars` are 'width height' pairs (width = skeleton-specific proportion, height = a dimension). All design values live here, never in the SDK.
skeleton:
  gap:
    $value: "{space.2}"
  fill:
    $value: "{color.surface.sunken}"
  radius:
    $value: "{radius.md}"
  barRadius:
    $value: "{radius.sm}"
  image:
    $value:
      minHeight: 10rem
  card:
    $value:
      padding: "{space.4}"
      bars: [ 100% 7.5rem, 60% 1rem, 90% 0.75rem ]
  text:
    $value:
      bars: [ 80% 1rem, 100% 0.75rem, 95% 0.75rem, 70% 0.75rem ]
definition.semantic/text-styles.yaml:
$description: 'Composed text styles — named by purpose, matching the GLOBAL DESIGN SYSTEM token-for-token (size + line-height + letter-spacing + weight per role). Components reference these (e.g. "font": "headline.md"); each composes base/typography primitives.'
text:
  $type: typography
  display:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.display}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.display.md}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.bold}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.display}"
      letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.display}"
  headline:
    lg:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.display}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.headline.lg}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.headline}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.headline}"
    md:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.display}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.headline.md}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.headline}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.headline}"
    sm:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.display}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.headline.sm}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.headline}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.headline}"
  title:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.display}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.title.md}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.title}"
      letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.title}"
  body:
    lg:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.bodyLg}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.normal}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.body}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.body}"
    md:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.bodyMd}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.normal}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.body}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.body}"
    sm:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.bodySm}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.normal}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.body}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.body}"
  label:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.labelMd}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.medium}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.label}"
      letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.label}"
  caption:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.caption}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.normal}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.label}"
      letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.label}"
  button:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.bodyMd}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.body}"
      letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.button}"

  # An EYEBROW: the small label that names the group a section belongs to. Uppercase and
  # tracked, which reads as a label rather than as a quiet heading. `textTransform` lives
  # here because a text style resolves to CSS wholesale, and the closed style-key set
  # deliberately has no text-transform of its own.
  eyebrow:
    $value:
      fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
      fontSize: "{font.size.caption}"
      fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
      lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.label}"
      letterSpacing: 0.08em
      textTransform: uppercase

  # PROSE headings, the styles semantic/prose.json's heading map points at. Separate from
  # the UI scale above because the two want opposite things: a UI heading is placed by its
  # layout and must carry NO margins, while a heading inside a body of copy has nothing but
  # its own spacing to separate one section from the next. Mapping markdown at the UI scale
  # is what made long-form bodyCopy render as one unbroken column in every org.
  prose:
    # A `## Section`. The rule and the top margin are what turn a run of sections (a
    # product's benefits, a course's modules) into readable blocks rather than a wall.
    section:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.prose}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.headline.sm}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.headline}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.headline}"
        color: "{color.text.primary}"
        marginTop: "{space.8}"
        marginBottom: "{space.3}"
        paddingTop: "{space.5}"
        borderTop: "{border.width.thin} solid {color.border.subtle}"
    # A `### Sub-section`. Divides WITHIN a section, so no rule: a second horizontal line
    # would compete with the section break it sits under.
    subsection:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.prose}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.title.lg}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.title}"
        color: "{color.text.primary}"
        marginTop: "{space.6}"
        marginBottom: "{space.2}"
    # A `#### Label` and below. Smaller and quieter than the body it introduces, so it
    # reads as an eyebrow instead of competing with a subsection.
    label:
      $value:
        fontFamily: "{font.family.sans}"
        fontSize: "{font.size.bodyMd}"
        fontWeight: "{font.weight.semibold}"
        lineHeight: "{font.lineHeight.label}"
        letterSpacing: "{font.tracking.label}"
        color: "{color.text.tertiary}"
        marginTop: "{space.5}"
        marginBottom: "{space.1}"
definition.themes/dark.yaml:
$description: Dark theme — STARTER. Same semantic token NAMES as light.json (so components are unchanged), remapped to dark base values. Refine against a canonical dark palette when one exists — values here are reasonable inversions, not brand-official.
color:
  $type: color
  text:
    primary:
      $value: "{color.gray.50}"
    secondary:
      $value: "{color.gray.300}"
    tertiary:
      $value: "{color.gray.400}"
    inverse:
      $value: "{color.gray.900}"
  surface:
    base:
      $value: "{color.gray.900}"
    raised:
      $value: "{color.gray.800}"
    sunken:
      $value: "{color.gray.950}"
    inverse:
      $value: "{color.gray.100}"
  border:
    subtle:
      $value: "{color.gray.800}"
    strong:
      $value: "{color.gray.700}"
    accent:
      $description: The CTA outline colour. Defaults to this theme's strong border; a brand that wants its CTAs to stand out overrides THIS one token.
      $value: "{color.border.strong}"
  action:
    primary:
      $value: "{color.primary.500}"
    primary-hover:
      $value: "{color.primary.400}"
    primary-active:
      $value: "{color.primary.300}"
    primary-text:
      $value: "{color.gray.950}"
    subtle:
      $value: "{color.primary.900}"
  status:
    success:
      $value: "{color.success.400}"
    success-subtle:
      $value: "{color.success.900}"
    success-border:
      $value: "{color.success.900}"
    success-text:
      $value: "{color.success.400}"
    error:
      $value: "{color.error.500}"
    warning:
      $value: "{color.warning.500}"
    info:
      $value: "{color.info.500}"
  overlay:
    scrim:
      $value: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(0,0,0,0.45), rgba(0,0,0,0.05), transparent)

$description: Light theme — the semantic color layer. Components reference THESE names; aliases point at base/color.json. Seeded from colors.css semantic vars.
color:

    secondary:

  surface:

    raised:
      $value: "{color.white}"
    sunken:

    inverse:
      $value: "{color.gray.800}"
  border:
    subtle:
      $value: "{color.gray.200}"
    strong:
      $value: "{color.gray.300}"
    accent:
      $description: The CTA outline colour. Defaults to this theme's strong border; a brand that wants its CTAs to stand out overrides THIS one token.
      $value: "{color.border.strong}"
  action:
    primary:
      $value: "{color.primary.500}"
    primary-hover:
      $value: "{color.primary.600}"
    primary-active:
      $value: "{color.primary.700}"
    primary-text:
      $value: "{color.white}"
    subtle:
      $value: "{color.primary.50}"
  status:
    success:
      $value: "{color.success.500}"
    success-subtle:
      $value: "{color.success.50}"
    success-border:
      $value: "{color.success.200}"
    success-text:
